backlog.spec: In phys_one, add these descriptors to vals: Descriptors.FractionCSP3, Descriptors.NumAromaticRings, Descriptors.HeavyAtomCount, Descriptors.NumHeteroatoms, rdMolDescriptors.CalcNumAmideBonds (import from rdkit.Chem), plus a formal-charge count (the number of atoms with nonzero GetFormalCharge) and the count of carboxylic acid groups, matched with the SMARTS 'C(=O)[OH]'. Raise the Ridge alpha to 3.0.
backlog.title: Richer linear baseline with more descriptors

backlog.spec: Replace the Ridge baseline in fit_predict with a more robust pipeline: fit sklearn QuantileTransformer(n_quantiles=min(200, len(train)), output_distribution='normal') on the six physchem descriptors plus aromatic fraction (the phys() output), then fit HuberRegressor(epsilon=1.35, alpha=1e-3, max_iter=1000) on the transformed features to predict y. Use the fitted model's predictions as base_tr and base_te in place of the Ridge predictions, leaving the XGBoost residual stages unchanged.
backlog.title: Robust linear baseline with quantile-transformed physchem features

backlog.spec: After featurizing the train set, compute for each Morgan count column the number of training molecules with a nonzero value. Keep only the columns with count of at least 5 (all descriptor columns are kept). Apply the same column mask to the test features. Fit both XGB stages on the reduced matrix, which cuts noise columns and lets colsample_bytree=0.3 select better.
backlog.title: Drop rare fingerprint bits

backlog.spec: Keep the Ridge baseline and the two-stage XGB. Also fit a CatBoostRegressor (loss_function='MAE', iterations=1500, learning_rate=0.03, depth=6, rsm=0.2, random_seed=seed, thread_count=8, verbose=0) on Xtr against the residual y - base_tr. Return base_te + 0.5*xgb_pred + 0.5*cat_pred.
backlog.title: Average XGB with a CatBoost model on the same residual

backlog.spec: Keep the two-stage XGBoost recipe, but also append the out-of-fold base prediction as one extra column of Xtr and Xte. Use 5-fold KFold(shuffle=True, random_state=seed) on the training fold to produce out-of-fold base predictions for Xtr, and fit the base on the full training fold for Xte. Still fit the residual target y - base_tr, so the base is both an input and an offset. This lets trees learn where the linear base is over- or under-confident.
backlog.title: Physchem base prediction as an XGBoost input feature

backlog.spec: In featurize_one, keep only the 2048 Morgan count features and the six physchem values already used by the base. Remove the full Descriptors.descList block (about 200 columns) from the XGBoost input matrix. The Ridge base and the two-stage XGBoost recipe are otherwise unchanged. The goal is to test whether the full descriptor set adds noise to the boosted residual model, and to cut feature computation time.
backlog.title: Drop the full RDKit descriptor block from the residual features

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, after building Xtr and Xte, compute for the first N_BITS columns (the Morgan counts) how many training rows are nonzero. Keep only the Morgan columns that are nonzero in at least 3 training molecules, and keep all descriptor columns. Apply the same column mask to Xte before the XGB fits.
backlog.title: Drop Morgan bits seen in fewer than 3 training molecules

backlog.spec: After featurizing, remove the fingerprint columns that are nonzero in fewer than 10 training molecules, and drop constant descriptors. Fit on the training set only. This reduces noise features so colsample picks more informative columns.
backlog.title: Feature selection by variance and importance

backlog.spec: Wrap the two-stage XGB fit in a loop over 3 seeds (seed, seed+1, seed+2), each with its own random_state and subsample=0.7. Average the three stage2 predictions and add base_te. Keep n_jobs=8. Only the XGB part is repeated. The physchem ridge is fit once.
backlog.title: Seed-bagged two-stage model

backlog.spec: Replace the stage-2 objective 'reg:absoluteerror' with 'reg:pseudohubererror' and set huber_slope=0.5 (roughly a third of the target's spread, so most residuals sit in the quadratic region and only outliers are down-weighted linearly). Keep stage 1 (200 rounds reg:squarederror) and the warm start unchanged, keep n_estimators=400 and all other parameters identical. The evaluation metric is MAE, but a smooth loss gives better-behaved gradients than the constant +/-1 of L1 while still being robust, so this directly tests whether the accepted L1 stage is winning through robustness or through exact median targeting.
backlog.title: Pseudo-Huber second stage

backlog.spec: Append two extra fingerprint blocks to featurize_one, which currently returns Morgan counts (2048) concatenated with the full RDKit descriptor list: the Avalon count fingerprint (rdkit.Avalon.pyAvalonTools.GetAvalonCountFP with nBits=512, converted to a dense float32 array) and the ErG pharmacophore fingerprint (rdkit.Chem.rdReducedGraphs.GetErGFingerprint, 315 floats). Cache them in the same _CACHE entry. The model and the ridge base stay exactly as they are. This combination scored 0.3710 against the older single-stage incumbent, i.e. a small apparent gain that was never retested on top of the accepted two-stage residual fit, so this slot is specifically about whether the two effects add.
backlog.title: Avalon and ErG fingerprints inside the two-stage recipe

backlog.spec: Replace stage2's objective='reg:absoluteerror' with objective='reg:pseudohubererror' and huber_slope=0.5. Keep warm-starting from stage1 and n_estimators=400. This gives a smoother robust loss than pure MAE.
backlog.title: Pseudo-Huber objective for stage 2

backlog.spec: Train a CatBoostRegressor (loss_function MAE, depth 6, iterations 800, learning_rate 0.05, random_seed=seed, thread_count=8, verbose=0) on the same features and residual target y - base_tr. Average its prediction with the XGB prediction 50/50 and add base_te.
backlog.title: Add CatBoost to ensemble

backlog.spec: Compute the Morgan bit fingerprints (radius 2, 2048 bits) for the training and test molecules, and their pairwise Tanimoto similarity. For each test molecule, take the mean target of its k=5 most similar training molecules and append it as one feature column. For training molecules, compute the same feature with the self-match excluded, so there is no target leakage. Append this column to Xtr and Xte, then run the unchanged two-stage XGBoost recipe.
backlog.title: Leave-self-out Tanimoto nearest-neighbour target feature

backlog.spec: Keep the features, Ridge baseline and two-stage XGBoost structure. In fit_predict, train the two-stage model 5 times with seeds seed*10+k for k in 0..4 (different subsample and colsample draws, each with the same hyperparameters), and average the 5 stage2 test predictions before adding base_te. This reduces variance from the stochastic subsampling; keep the total runtime well under the 10-minute job limit.
backlog.title: Seed bagging of the boosted residual model

backlog.spec: Keep the Ridge baseline and the two-stage XGBoost residual model as they are. Add a LightGBM regressor (objective='l1', n_estimators=600, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=31, min_child_samples=10, colsample_bytree=0.3, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8, verbose=-1) fit on the same features and the same residual target y - base_tr. Return base_te plus the simple average of the XGBoost stage2 prediction and the LightGBM prediction.
backlog.title: LightGBM residual model averaged with XGBoost

backlog.spec: Also fit sklearn SVR(kernel='rbf', C=3.0, epsilon=0.05, gamma='scale') on the descriptor part of Xtr (the columns after N_BITS). Standardize these columns with a StandardScaler fit on train, then clip them to [-5,5]. Fit the SVR against the residual y - base_tr. Final prediction: base_te + 0.7*xgb_pred + 0.3*svr_pred.
backlog.title: Blend in an RBF-kernel SVR on scaled descriptors

backlog.spec: Set learning_rate=0.02 in the shared params, stage1 n_estimators=300 and stage2 n_estimators=600. Keep everything else unchanged. This tests a slower shrinkage within the two-stage recipe.
backlog.title: Learning-rate 0.02 with more rounds

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, replace Ridge(alpha=1.0) on the standardized physchem features with RidgeCV(alphas=np.logspace(-2, 3, 12)) fit on the training fold only. Keep everything else unchanged: the base prediction is still base_tr and base_te, and the two-stage XGBoost residual model is trained on y - base_tr. The alpha is chosen by RidgeCV's internal generalized cross-validation, so no test data is used.
backlog.title: RidgeCV alpha for the physchem base

backlog.spec: In stage 2 only, pass sample_weight to XGBRegressor.fit. Set w = 1/sqrt(n_heavy_atoms), normalized so that mean(w) = 1, where n_heavy_atoms is each training molecule's heavy-atom count, computed with rdkit. Stage 1 and the ridge base are unchanged. The aim is to stop the L1 residual fit from being dominated by the largest molecules, which may be least representative of the small-molecule test distribution.
backlog.title: Down-weight large molecules in the L1 stage

backlog.spec: Wrap the stage1+stage2 XGB fit in a loop over 5 sub-seeds (seed*10+k, k=0..4). Pass each sub-seed as random_state to both stages. Average the 5 stage2 predictions on Xte and add base_te. All other parameters stay the same.
backlog.title: Seed-bagged XGB ensemble

backlog.spec: In params, change colsample_bytree from 0.3 to 0.15. Add reg_lambda=5.0 and reg_alpha=0.5. Also change subsample from 0.8 to 0.7. Leave everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Lower XGB colsample and add L1/L2 regularization

backlog.spec: Change learning_rate to 0.015 and double the n_estimators (stage1 400, stage2 800) to get smoother boosting. Check that the run time stays within budget.
backlog.title: Lower learning rate with more trees

backlog.spec: After computing the final prediction base_te + stage2.predict(Xte), clip the returned array to [min(y) - 0.1*r, max(y) + 0.1*r], where r = max(y) - min(y) and y is the training fold target. This prevents extreme extrapolation for out-of-domain molecules, where the linear physchem base can give unrealistic values. Change nothing else.
backlog.title: Clip predictions to the training target range

backlog.spec: Keep the ECFP counts at radius 2. Also add a second Morgan count fingerprint built with rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator(radius=3, fpSize=1024, atomInvariantsGenerator=rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen()). Concatenate it in featurize_one before the descriptors. The model is unchanged.
backlog.title: Morgan radius 3 with feature-invariant (FCFP) counts added

backlog.spec: Replace the physchem Ridge base with a spline basis. Standardize the seven physchem features (TPSA, MolLogP, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, MolWt, NumRotatableBonds, aromatic fraction), then apply sklearn SplineTransformer(n_knots=4, degree=3, include_bias=False) fit on the training fold. Fit Ridge(alpha=3.0) on the spline features to get base_tr and base_te. The XGBoost two-stage residual model is unchanged and is trained on y - base_tr.
backlog.title: Spline-expanded physchem base

backlog.spec: Replace the two-stage XGB (squared error then absolute error warm start) with a single XGBRegressor using objective 'reg:pseudohubererror' (huber_slope=0.5) and 500 trees on y - base_tr. This tests whether the warm-start complexity is needed.
backlog.title: Huber-style single-stage XGB

backlog.spec: Add reg_lambda=5, reg_alpha=0.5, gamma=0.05 and min_child_weight=5 to the shared XGBoost params dict (both stages). Keep everything else the same. This tests stronger leaf and split regularization for the small dataset.
backlog.title: Stronger XGB regularization

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, replace the stage-2 XGBRegressor objective 'reg:absoluteerror' with 'reg:pseudohubererror' (huber_slope=0.5), keeping n_estimators=400 and the xgb_model=stage1.get_booster() continuation. Everything else stays unchanged. Pseudo-Huber has a smooth gradient near zero, which may give steadier leaf values than pure L1.
backlog.title: Pseudo-Huber stage two

memo: Helped: swapping RF for XGBoost with L1 loss (0.3828, -0.0589 vs the 0.4417 start). Adding a ridge on six RDKit physchem descriptors plus aromatic-atom features, with XGB fitting its residuals, gave 0.3755/0.3715. A two-stage XGB residual fit (200 rounds of squared-error, then L1) is the current incumbent at 0.3658/0.3652 over 2 runs. Noise-level or no gain (noise sd about 0.0037): bagged XGB 0.3793, 6-model ensemble 0.3795, winsorized targets 0.3727, Avalon+ErG 0.3710, LightGBM, CatBoost, GP, MLP, Tanimoto kernel ridge, MACCS, 3D shape, calibration, quantile correction, polynomial or sparse-L1 ridge bases. Tree and Morgan tuning looks saturated. Next: vary the two-stage recipe (round counts, learning rate, Huber loss for stage two), combine small gains with it (bagging, Avalon/ErG, winsorizing), and add polarity/ionization descriptors (TPSA, HBD, charge) to the ridge. Avoid specs that abort at the engine.
